Lessons.Title: Applying the Quadratic Formula (Part 1)
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: set up contextual quadratic equations that may be difficult to solve by inspection, use the formula appropriately and reject mathematical solutions inconsistent with real-world constraints. First-party Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 7 Lesson 17 teacher https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/7/17/preparation.html and student https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/7/17/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The source discusses why a real discriminant matters and when other methods may be simpler.

Original idealized foam-ball height h(t)=−5t²+20t+2 metres for t≥0 until landing. Ask when it reaches17 metres: −5t²+20t+2=17, so −5t²+20t−15=0; divide−5 to obtain t²−4t+3=0. Quadratic formula with a1,b−4,c3 yields D16−12=4 and t=(4±2)/2=1 or3 seconds.

The height function has vertex at t2, maximum h(2)=−20+40+2=22 metres. A target30 metres cannot be reached; equation h(t)=30 has no real roots and would give negative discriminant. Both 1s and3s are valid flight times for reaching17m; they correspond to rising and falling stages.

Student task: graph height and horizontal target levels, solve h=17 using formula and compare to factoring, explain impossibility of h=30, and articulate limitations of the gravity approximation. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 each for model equation, discriminant/roots, contextual selection and mathematical explanation.

KeyConcepts.Title: Impossible target
KeyConcepts.Definition: A target greater than the model maximum has no real time solution.
